definition: The basic laws of a country.
examples: The US Constitution was written in 1787.
This right is in the constitution.
The new constitution protects free speech.

definition: The act of making people obey a law.
examples: He works in law enforcement.
There's strict enforcement of the speed limit.
Enforcement of the rule is weak.

spanish.definition: Acto de hacer que la gente obedezca una ley.

definition: To kill animals for food; the killing of many people.
examples: The farmer slaughtered a pig.
The slaughter of civilians shocked the world.
Cattle are slaughtered at this plant.

spanish.definition: Matar animales para comer; asesinato de muchas personas.

definition: A person who helps someone commit a crime.
examples: Police arrested his accomplice.
She was an accomplice to the robbery.
He had an accomplice inside the bank.

spanish.definition: Persona que ayuda a cometer un delito.

definition: Protection given to someone who left their country for safety.
examples: The family asked for asylum in the US.
He was given political asylum.
Many people are seeking asylum here.

spanish.definition: Protección para alguien que dejó su país por seguridad.

definition: A formal fight between two people.
examples: He challenged him to a duel.
Hamilton died in a duel.
The two men fought a duel at dawn.

definition: The act of getting rid of something; a kitchen sink machine.
examples: The garbage disposal is broken.
The city handles waste disposal.
I'm at your disposal.

spanish.definition: Acto de deshacerse de algo; máquina en el fregadero.

definition: A group of signs that show a medical problem.
examples: He has Down syndrome.
She suffers from a rare syndrome.
Doctors don't know what causes the syndrome.

spanish.definition: Grupo de señales que muestran un problema médico.

definition: To attract someone with something; an object for catching fish.
examples: The ads lured people to the store.
He lured the dog with a piece of meat.
She tied a lure to the line.

spanish.definition: Atraer a alguien con algo; objeto para pescar.

definition: True for or used by everyone.
examples: Music is a universal language.
Everyone wants universal health care.
Love is a universal feeling.

definition: To punish someone for a wrong done to you.
examples: He wanted to avenge his brother's death.
She swore to avenge her family.
The hero avenged his father.

spanish.definition: Castigar a alguien por un daño que te hizo.

definition: Using science to solve crimes.
examples: The police found forensic evidence.
She's a forensic scientist.
The forensic team is at the house.

spanish.definition: Que usa la ciencia para resolver delitos.

definition: A long trip, usually by sea.
examples: Columbus made his first voyage in 1492.
The Titanic sank on its first voyage.
Have a good voyage.

definition: The yellow liquid that leaves your body.
examples: The doctor asked for a urine sample.
The test checks your urine.
The hallway smells of urine.

spanish.definition: Líquido amarillo que sale del cuerpo.

definition: A person in charge of a group of workers.
examples: He's the foreman at the factory.
The foreman told us to go home.
Ask the foreman about the schedule.

spanish.definition: Persona a cargo de un grupo de trabajadores.

definition: A time of testing a worker or a criminal.
examples: He's on probation for two years.
New employees have three months of probation.
She's a probation officer.

spanish.definition: Tiempo de prueba de un trabajador o un delincuente.

definition: A robber, often in a group.
examples: Bandits attacked the train.
The mountains are full of bandits.
The bandit stole their horses.

definition: The smallest piece in chess; a person used by others.
examples: He moved his pawn forward.
She took my guitar to a pawn shop.
We're only pawns in their game.

spanish.definition: La pieza más pequeña del ajedrez; persona usada por otros.

definition: A suggestion or an offer.
examples: I have a proposition for you.
It's a very expensive proposition.
Voters said no to Proposition 8.

definition: A large strong building for defense.
examples: The old fortress stands on the hill.
The soldiers defended the fortress.
We visited a fortress in Cartagena.

spanish.definition: Edificio grande y fuerte para defenderse.

definition: Connected to a navy.
examples: He's a naval officer.
There's a naval base nearby.
They won a great naval battle.

definition: Official permission; a sale of goods at low prices.
examples: The pilot got clearance to land.
She has security clearance.
All shoes are on clearance.

spanish.definition: Permiso oficial; venta de productos a precios bajos.

definition: The act of leaving a job.
examples: He handed in his resignation.
Her resignation surprised us all.
The minister announced his resignation.

definition: Very upset; extremely funny.
examples: She became hysterical after the crash.
That show is hysterical!
Don't get hysterical.

definition: An unusual fact or event.
examples: Rain is a natural phenomenon.
The song became a world phenomenon.
It's a strange new phenomenon.

definition: Careful about what you say.
examples: He's very discreet about his work.
Please be discreet.
They made a discreet phone call.

definition: An official study of a problem; a spacecraft for research.
examples: The police started a probe into the deaths.
A space probe landed on Mars.
There's a federal probe of the company.

spanish.definition: Estudio oficial de un problema; nave para investigar.

definition: A fight against a government or against rules.
examples: The king ended the rebellion.
Teenage rebellion is normal.
A rebellion broke out in the south.

spanish.definition: Pelea contra un gobierno o contra las reglas.

definition: The act of secretly damaging something.
examples: Police think the fire was sabotage.
He was arrested for sabotage.
The crash may have been an act of sabotage.

spanish.definition: Acto de dañar algo en secreto.

definition: A thin cloth that covers a woman's face.
examples: The bride wore a long veil.
She lifted her veil.
Some women wear a veil in public.

spanish.definition: Tela delgada que cubre la cara de una mujer.

definition: A safe place.
examples: The park is a bird sanctuary.
The church offered sanctuary to the family.
My garden is my sanctuary.

definition: A poor farmer of the past.
examples: The peasants worked the land.
He was the son of a peasant.
The peasants rose up against the king.

definition: Excellent.
examples: The food was superb.
She did a superb job.
He's a superb cook.

definition: Protection from danger.
examples: We took refuge in a cave.
People found refuge in the church.
The island is a wildlife refuge.

definition: Something you do very well; a special dish.
examples: Fish is the chef's specialty.
Her specialty is heart surgery.
What's the specialty of the house?

spanish.definition: Algo que haces muy bien; plato especial.

definition: Based on reason.
examples: There's a rational explanation.
Let's be rational about this.
He made a rational decision.

definition: The killing of many people.
examples: The massacre shocked the country.
Hundreds died in the massacre.
The town still remembers the massacre.

definition: Protected from a disease.
examples: I'm immune to chicken pox.
He has a weak immune system.
Nobody is immune from criticism.

definition: A small bomb thrown by hand.
examples: The soldier threw a grenade.
The grenade exploded in the street.
They found an old grenade in the field.

spanish.definition: Bomba pequeña que se lanza con la mano.

definition: A room for a baby; a place that sells plants.
examples: We painted the nursery yellow.
I bought these roses at a nursery.
She sang old nursery rhymes.

spanish.definition: Cuarto para un bebé; lugar que vende plantas.

definition: A flat area outside a building.
examples: We had breakfast on the terrace.
The hotel has a large terrace.
The apartment has a roof terrace.

spanish.definition: Área plana afuera de un edificio.

definition: Getting involved when you aren't wanted; noise on a radio.
examples: I don't want any interference from you.
There's interference on the line.
The government denied any interference.

spanish.definition: Meterse cuando no te quieren; ruido en una radio.

definition: The person who did something wrong.
examples: The police caught the culprit.
Sugar is the real culprit.
Who's the culprit?

definition: Unfair treatment.
examples: We have to fight injustice.
It was a terrible injustice.
He has seen a lot of injustice.

definition: A break in a bone; to break a bone.
examples: She has a fracture in her arm.
He fractured his leg skiing.
The X-ray showed a small fracture.

spanish.definition: Rotura en un hueso; romperse un hueso.

definition: The state of being crazy.
examples: The lawyer argued insanity.
This is pure insanity.
He lived on the edge of insanity.

definition: Extreme pain.
examples: He was in agony after the fall.
She screamed in agony.
Waiting for the results was agony.

definition: A small, simple, poor house.
examples: They lived in a wooden shack.
There's an old shack by the lake.
The storm destroyed the little shack.

definition: An area of land where dead people are buried.
examples: There's an old graveyard behind the church.
The kids were afraid of the graveyard.
He works the graveyard shift.

spanish.definition: Tierra donde se entierra a los muertos.

definition: Complete.
examples: It was an utter disaster.
He's an utter fool.
She looked at him in utter surprise.

definition: To allow someone to leave a hospital or the army.
examples: She was discharged from the hospital today.
He was discharged from the army.
They're discharging him tomorrow.

spanish.definition: Permitirle a alguien salir de un hospital o del ejército.

definition: The state of being forced to live outside your country.
examples: The leader lived in exile for ten years.
He died in exile.
Her family went into exile in Spain.

spanish.definition: Estado de ser obligado a vivir fuera de tu país.

definition: A small flying machine with no pilot.
examples: He took the photo with a drone.
The drone flew over the beach.
The army uses drones.

definition: Something that shows respect for someone.
examples: The concert was a tribute to the singer.
He paid tribute to his mother.
This statue is a tribute to the soldiers.

spanish.definition: Algo que muestra respeto por alguien.

definition: Bad luck.
examples: I had the misfortune to meet him.
He suffered a lot of misfortune.
Don't laugh at other people's misfortune.

definition: Very detailed and complicated.
examples: They made elaborate plans.
She wore an elaborate dress.
It was an elaborate lie.

definition: To order someone to come.
examples: The boss summoned me to his office.
She was summoned to court.
He's summoning his team.

definition: Alone.
examples: He lives a solitary life.
She took a solitary walk on the beach.
He was put in solitary confinement.

definition: A round roof.
examples: The church has a gold dome.
The Capitol dome is in Washington.
The team plays in a dome.

definition: Loose; not busy.
examples: The rope is slack.
Business is slack in January.
Her mouth went slack.

definition: A family that rules for a long time.
examples: The Ming dynasty ruled China.
The Kennedys are a political dynasty.
The team built a dynasty in the 1990s.

spanish.definition: Familia que gobierna por mucho tiempo.

definition: Connected to mental illness.
examples: He's in a psychiatric hospital.
She needs psychiatric help.
The court ordered a psychiatric exam.

definition: An organization or a business.
examples: This is a family establishment.
He's the owner of the establishment.
We visited an educational establishment.

definition: A small imaginary person in stories.
examples: Snow White lived with seven dwarfs.
The dwarf carried a small axe.
In the movie, a dwarf helps the hero.

spanish.definition: Persona pequeña imaginaria de los cuentos.

definition: A person paid to clean a house or a hotel.
examples: The housekeeper cleaned our room.
She works as a housekeeper in a hotel.
They hired a housekeeper.

spanish.definition: Persona a la que le pagan por limpiar una casa o un hotel.

definition: To hate someone very much.
examples: He despises liars.
I despise this job.
She despised him for what he did.

definition: To wait for something.
examples: We await your reply.
A surprise awaited us at home.
He's awaiting trial.

definition: Perfect happiness.
examples: A hot bath is pure bliss.
The couple lived in bliss.
Ignorance is bliss.

definition: A strong feeling that someone is worthless.
examples: He looked at me with contempt.
She treated them with contempt.
He was charged with contempt of court.

spanish.definition: Sentimiento fuerte de que alguien no vale nada.

definition: A small separate space.
examples: Put your bag in the overhead compartment.
The glove compartment is full of maps.
The suitcase has a secret compartment.

definition: A person who watches for danger; a place with a view.
examples: Be on the lookout for a red car.
We stopped at a lookout on the mountain.
He stood as a lookout at the door.

spanish.definition: Persona que vigila; lugar con vista.

definition: A magic liquid.
examples: The witch made a love potion.
He drank the magic potion.
The kids mixed a pretend potion.

definition: Impossible to defeat.
examples: The team seemed invincible.
Young people think they're invincible.
He felt invincible after the win.

definition: A tube that carries blood from the heart; a major road.
examples: A blocked artery caused his heart attack.
The doctors repaired the artery.
This highway is the main artery of the city.

spanish.definition: Tubo que lleva sangre desde el corazón; carretera principal.

definition: Strange and frightening.
examples: There was an eerie silence.
The empty school felt eerie.
I heard an eerie sound at night.

definition: A formal agreement.
examples: The two countries signed a pact.
We made a pact to stay friends forever.
They broke the pact.

definition: Connected to young people; childish.
examples: He spent time in juvenile prison.
Your behavior is juvenile.
The city has a juvenile court.

definition: Great love or loyalty.
examples: Her devotion to her family is amazing.
He showed great devotion to his wife.
The dog's devotion touched everyone.

definition: A person who gives secret information to the police.
examples: The police used an informant.
He's a police informant.
An informant told them about the drugs.

spanish.definition: Persona que da información secreta a la policía.

definition: Done by a group.
examples: It was a collective decision.
We all have a collective responsibility.
The workers made a collective effort.

definition: A statement about the future.
examples: The prophecy came true.
An old prophecy warned of a flood.
She believed in the prophecy.

definition: A short burst of air or smoke.
examples: A puff of smoke came from the chimney.
He took a puff on his cigar.
Blow a little puff of air.

spanish.definition: Salida corta de aire o humo.

definition: A strong light used as a signal.
examples: The lighthouse beacon guided the ship.
The fire was a beacon in the dark.
She's a beacon of hope.

definition: To make something lighter or less heavy.
examples: She lightened her hair.
He told a joke to lighten the mood.
We're lightening our bags for the flight.

spanish.definition: Hacer algo más claro o menos pesado.

definition: Connected to the North or South Pole.
examples: Polar bears live in the Arctic.
Polar ice is melting.
We saw a polar bear at the zoo.

spanish.definition: Relacionado con el Polo Norte o el Polo Sur.

definition: A small opening that lets air in or out.
examples: There's a vent in the ceiling.
Air comes through the vent.
The smoke went out the vent.

spanish.definition: Abertura pequeña que deja entrar o salir aire.

definition: Connected to a careful plan.
examples: It was a tactical mistake.
The police wore tactical gear.
The coach made a tactical change.

definition: The written text of a movie.
examples: She wrote the screenplay for the movie.
He won an Oscar for best screenplay.
I'm writing a screenplay.

definition: A long, sharp tooth.
examples: The snake has two fangs.
The vampire showed his fangs.
The dog bared its fangs.

definition: Behind the stage in a theater.
examples: We went backstage to meet the band.
The actors waited backstage.
I have a backstage pass.

spanish.definition: Detrás del escenario de un teatro.

definition: The oldest in a family.
examples: She's the eldest of five children.
My eldest son lives in Madrid.
His eldest sister is a doctor.

spanish.definition: El de más edad en una familia.

definition: A large rock in space.
examples: An asteroid killed the dinosaurs.
The asteroid passed close to the Earth.
Scientists are tracking a new asteroid.

definition: A person who delivers packages.
examples: The courier brought the documents.
We sent it by courier.
She works as a bike courier.

definition: A short phrase with a belief or a rule.
examples: Our family motto is simple: never give up.
The school motto is in Latin.
Work hard: that's my motto.

spanish.definition: Frase corta con una creencia o una regla.

definition: A small soft green plant on rocks and trees.
examples: Moss grows on the north side of the tree.
The stones are covered in moss.
There's moss on the roof.

spanish.definition: Planta pequeña, suave y verde en rocas y árboles.

definition: The end of a sleeve.
examples: There's a stain on my shirt cuff.
She rolled up her cuffs.
The cuffs on this shirt are too tight.

definition: A line of color; a series of wins or losses.
examples: She has a blue streak in her hair.
The team is on a winning streak.
There's a streak of paint on the wall.

spanish.definition: Línea de color; serie de triunfos o derrotas.

definition: To walk or travel with no plan.
examples: Cows roam on the hills.
The kids roamed the neighborhood.
Wild horses are roaming the plains.

definition: To love and take care of something.
examples: I cherish our time together.
She cherished her old photos.
He's cherishing every moment with his son.

definition: An expert; a spiritual teacher.
examples: He's a computer guru.
She's a fitness guru with a million followers.
The guru taught them to meditate.
